'''Futami-ga-ura''' is a sub-bay or inlet of [[Ise Bay]] in [[Japan]], where the [[Isuzu River]] enters the bay.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Japan Atlas: Futamiura in Ise |url=https://web-japan.org/atlas/nature/nat09.html |access-date=2023-03-09 |website=web-japan.org}}</ref><ref name="gn1863740">[{{Geonameslink|gnid=1863740|name=futami-ura}} Futami-ura] sa [{{Geonamesabout}} Geonames.org (cc-by)]; post updated 2013-10-07; database download sa 2017-02-07</ref> It is located in [[Mie prefecture]], in the southern part of the country, 300&nbsp;km southwest of [[Tokyo]].

It is where the famous [[Meoto Iwa]] rocks are found.<ref name="organizacion-de-convenciones-de-turismo-de-ise-shima-2021a" />

{{Location map|Japan|width=300|float=right|caption=Futami-ga-ura in Japan|label=Futami-ura|position=right|background=white|lat_deg=34.50929|lon_deg=136.7909}}

==Description==
Futami-ga-ura is a [[River delta|delta]] formed at the mouth of the [[Isuzu River]] that flows into [[Ise Bay]]. It is part of [[Ise-Shima National Park]] that has been designated a {{Ill|national scenic spot|ja|名勝}}, and has been selected as one of {{Ill|Japan's 100 best beaches|ja|日本の渚百選}}. It has sometimes served as a site for ritual purification (''[[misogi]]'') prior to worshiping at [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name="http-2014a">[http://www.jingukaikan.jp/sukeikai/imgs_mimosuso/55.pdf Archived copy] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141121044856/http://www.jingukaikan.jp/sukeikai/imgs_mimosuso/55.pdf |date=2014-11-21 }}</ref>

A rock formation called [[Meoto Iwa]], which is within the precincts of [[Futami Okitama Shrine]] in Tateishizaki, is a well-known geological feature with significance to [[Shinto]] devotees.<ref name="organizacion-de-convenciones-de-turismo-de-ise-shima-2021a">{{Cite web |title=Futami Okitama Jinja(Wedded Rocks) |url=https://www.iseshima-kanko.jp/en/see-and-do/1292 |access-date=28 September 2021 |publisher=Organización de Convenciones de Turismo de Ise Shima |language=en}}</ref>{{Tone inline|date=June 2022}}

==Climate==
The climate is temperate. The average temperature is 14&nbsp;°C. The warmest month is July, at 23&nbsp;°C, and the coldest January, at 5&nbsp;°C.<ref name="nasa">{{Cite web |title=NASA Earth Observations Data Set Index |url=http://neo.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/dataset_index.php |access-date=30 January 2016 |publisher=NASA |archive-date=6 August 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130806035941/http://neo.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/dataset_index.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> The average rainfall is 2,387 millimeters per year. The wettest month is June, with 316 millimeters of rain, and the wettest January, with 60 millimeters.<ref name="nasarain">{{Cite web |title=NASA Earth Observations: Rainfall (1 month - TRMM) |url=http://neo.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/view.php?datasetId=TRMM_3B43M |access-date=30 January 2016 |publisher=NASA/Tropical Rainfall Monitoring Mission |archive-date=29 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190629172738/https://neo.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/view.php?datasetId=TRMM_3B43M |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Futaminoura Beach ==
Futami beach was opened in 1881 ( Meiji 15) by the first [[Surgeon general]], [[Matsumoto Ryōjun]], and was designated by the Director of the Ministry of Home Affairs, Sanitation Bureau, Nagayo in 1882 (Meiji 16), the first officially recognized beach in Japan. It is said that [[Emperor Taishō|Emperor Taisho]] also trained in swimming when he was a child. At that time, the sea bathing was for medical purposes (bath digging), and there were cold baths that went into the sea and hot baths that were soaked in seawater warmed by a bathtub on the beach. Including, the inn town that sings Shioyuji was formed<ref name="http-2014a" />

== Guest house ==
There is a guest house {{Ill|Hinjitsukan|ja|賓日館}} located in the area. It was designated a tangible cultural property designated by Mie Prefecture on March 17, 2004.  It was designated a national important cultural property on June 29, 2010 .<ref>{{cite web |url=http://hinjitsukan.com/about.html |title=About に何も見つかりません |website=hinjitsukan.com |access-date=30 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190714035618/http://hinjitsukan.com/about.html |archive-date=14 July 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref>{{Verify source|date=June 2022}}
